title: Release audit: In `_quoted_binding`, after a quoted label and whitespace, a bare next token ret
summary: After skipping the gap, bind a bare value using the same `_span`/`_descriptor_span` and prose/no-value guard used for unquoted labels; add tests for single- and double-quoted labels followed by whitespace and an unquoted value, including display and retained state.
requirements: After a quoted label, whitespace and a bare unquoted value, the binding is treated as a credential binding and the value is masked in the output shown to the user.
Single-quoted labels and double-quoted labels are treated identically in that detection.

A quoted word that is not followed by a value, such as a quoted word at the end of a line or one followed by punctuation, is not treated as a credential binding and is left unchanged.

plan_goal: Forgel Code: interactive agent client instead of a command wrapper

result.summary: Closed the quoted-label gap in credential masking in `forgel_code/interactive.py`. `_quoted_binding` previously bound a value to a quoted label only through a separator (`'token': abc`) or a quoted run (`'token' 'abc'`) and returned None for anything else, so a quoted label followed by whitespace and a bare unquoted value (`'token' abc123`, `"password" hunter2`) left the secret visible. It now inspects the token after the closing quote: an authorization-scheme word still routes to `_scheme_value` (scheme visible, credential masked), a copula routes to `_copula_span` (`the 'token' is VALUE`), a prose/narrative word still means the label is only mentioned, and any other token is masked when it carries value markers or closes the clause. Clause closing is decided by a new helper `_closes_clause`, together with two new constants `_INLINE_WHITESPACE` and `_CLAUSE_END`, so a bare value at the end of the line or in front of punctuation is masked while a quoted word followed only by punctuation, or by a word that continues the sentence, stays unchanged. Single-quoted and double-quoted labels travel the same code path, so both behave identically, and the previously working forms (separator, quoted value, unquoted label with a bare value, unchanged secret-free output) keep their behaviour and their visible placeholder. No existing test was touched; new coverage lives in `tests/test_redact_quoted_bare.py` (10 tests, 37 subtests) covering single- and double-quoted bare values, clause-ending values, the preserved separator/quoted-value/unquoted-label forms, quoted words without a value, secret-free text, and idempotence with exactly one marker. The full suite passes: `python -m pytest -q` -> 334 passed, 363 subtests passed.
assumptions: A bare value after a quoted label ends at the same boundary as a bare value after an unquoted label: whitespace, with trailing clause punctuation left visible.
A token after a quoted label that carries value markers (digit, mixed case or value punctuation) is treated as the value even when a word follows it, mirroring the unquoted-label rule.
A quoted word followed by an ordinary word that continues the sentence is not a binding, so ordinary prose about a quoted label stays readable.
The masking placeholder stays `[redacted]` and quotation marks around a quoted value stay visible, unchanged from today.
No CHANGELOG entry was added: the specification lists producing or updating user documentation about masking as out of scope.

checks.criterion: A line made of a single-quoted label, whitespace and a bare value has the value masked in the produced output.
No existing test was weakened, removed or modified to obtain the pass.

review.summary: The change closes the quoted-label gap in credential masking: `_quoted_binding` no longer stops at the separator/quoted-run branches but also evaluates the bare word after a quoted label and reuses the existing binding helpers (`_scheme_value`, `_copula_span`, `_carries_markers`, `_span`), so a quoted label followed by a bare value is masked with the same placeholder and the same value boundaries as an unquoted label. A new `_closes_clause` helper and two constants (`_INLINE_WHITESPACE`, `_CLAUSE_END`) keep a plain word that merely continues the sentence from being treated as a value, and quoted words with nothing after them (end of line, punctuation) stay untouched, so unrelated output is unchanged. Both quote styles route through the same code path. The added test module covers every acceptance criterion including idempotency and preservation of the already-working forms, no existing test was edited or removed, and QA reports the full suite, the environment test and the acceptance checks passing on a clean worktree with only the two task files committed. The earlier masking outcomes for separators, quoted values and unquoted labels are preserved; handling of an auth-scheme or copula word between the quoted label and its value is an extension that follows the same leak-prevention intent and does not contradict any acceptance criterion.

requirements.requirement: After a quoted label, whitespace and a bare unquoted value, the binding is treated as a credential binding and the value is masked.
requirements.note: The final branch of `_quoted_binding` resolves the bare token after `_skip_gap` and returns its span, so the value is replaced by the existing `[redacted]` placeholder; verified by the masked-output acceptance check and the new quoted-bare tests.

requirements.requirement: Single-quoted and double-quoted labels are treated identically in that detection.
requirements.note: Both quote styles reach `_quoted_binding` after `_label_quote_end`; there is no quote-specific branch, and the new tests cover each style for the bare-value case.

requirements.requirement: A quoted label followed by a separator and a value is still masked.
requirements.note: The separator branch is untouched and still runs before the new code; covered by the existing quoted-label separator tests and the new regression tests.

requirements.requirement: A quoted label followed by a quoted value is still masked.
requirements.note: The `_QUOTE_PAIRS` branch is unchanged and precedes the new logic; covered by existing and new tests.

requirements.requirement: An unquoted label followed by a bare value is still masked.
requirements.note: The unquoted path is not modified; the change only adds a branch in `_quoted_binding`, and the suite passes.

requirements.requirement: A quoted word with no value after it (end of line, punctuation) is not masked.
requirements.note: At end of text `_quoted_binding` returns early, and `_label_end` returns None when punctuation follows, so such quoted words stay untouched; the new tests assert this for `'token'`, `'token'.` and comma cases.

requirements.requirement: Output that contains no credential binding is returned unchanged.
requirements.note: The new logic is gated by secret-label recognition and by `_is_prose`/`_carries_markers`/`_closes_clause`, and the new no-binding tests plus the full suite pass.
